How Affirm makes
money from stores

lines.text: Your 0% Affirm plan? Often, the store pays for it.
lines.say: Your zero percent Affirm plan? Often, the store pays for it.

lines.text: In fiscal 2026, store fees hit about $1.15B.
lines.say: In fiscal twenty twenty-six, store fees hit about one point one five billion.

lines.text: That's about 2.3% of $50.2B spent through Affirm.
lines.say: That's about two point three percent of fifty point two billion spent through Affirm.

lines.text: At that average, a $2,000 laptop sends about $46 to Affirm. The store keeps $1,954.
lines.say: At that average, a two thousand dollar laptop sends about forty-six dollars to Affirm. The store keeps nineteen hundred fifty-four.

lines.text: Twist: Affirm's 10-K says fees are generally bigger on 0% APR loans, lower on interest-bearing ones.
lines.say: Twist: Affirm's ten K says fees are generally bigger on zero percent A P R loans, lower on interest-bearing ones.

lines.text: No interest for you? The store covers more of the cost.

post.title: Affirm's other business: the fee stores pay
post.ig:
When you pay with Affirm, the store pays Affirm a fee too.
Store fees (merchant network revenue) were about $1.15B in fiscal 2026, the year to June 30, 2026.
That's about 2.3% of the $50.2B spent through Affirm, per its 10-K.
Affirm's 10-K says stores generally pay bigger fees on 0% APR loans.
Sources: Affirm Form 10-K filings, fiscal 2021-2026.
News and education, not financial advice.
